name: Language containment
summary: Decide whether every word accepted by one automaton is accepted by another. For nondeterministic Büchi automata it is PSPACE-complete; for a deterministic right side it is polynomial.

name: Nim
summary: Take-away game on heaps, solved by the XOR of heap sizes (Bouton's theorem).

name: Horn clause
summary: A clause with at most one positive literal. Definite clauses (facts and rules) have exactly one, and goal clauses have none. Sets of definite clauses always have a least Herbrand model.

name: Dagum-Luby theorem
aliases: NP-hardness of approximate Bayesian network inference
summary: With evidence, approximating P(X = x | e) in a Bayesian network within any absolute error below 1/2 is NP-hard. A relative approximation is NP-hard even with no evidence.

name: Marginal likelihood
summary: p(D | M), the probability of the data under a model with its parameters averaged over the prior. Ratios of it are Bayes factors; Laplace and BIC approximate it.

name: Focal loss
summary: The loss -α_t (1 - p_t)^γ log(p_t): cross-entropy scaled down for examples the model already gets right, so training focuses on hard, rare ones. γ = 0 gives cross-entropy.

name: Error-correcting output codes
summary: Give each class a codeword, train one binary classifier per code bit, and decode the outputs to the nearest codeword. Row distance d corrects floor((d-1)/2) errors.

name: Experience replay
summary: Keep the last N transitions in a circular buffer and train on minibatches drawn uniformly from it, so that each sample is reused and consecutive updates are less correlated.

name: Gradient temporal-difference learning
summary: Linear TD methods that do stochastic gradient descent on the projected Bellman error, with a second weight vector. GTD2 and TDC converge off-policy, where plain TD can diverge.

name: Wake-sleep algorithm
summary: Trains a generative model and a recognition model in turn: the wake phase fits the generative model to data inferred by recognition, the sleep phase fits recognition to dreams.

name: VC dimension
summary: The size of the largest set of points on which a binary hypothesis class realizes all labelings. It is finite exactly when the class is PAC learnable.

name: Value function approximation
summary: Represent a value function as Phi theta, a function of features. On-policy linear TD finds the fixed point of the projected Bellman equation, A theta = b, near the best fit.

name: Difference bound matrix
summary: A matrix of bounds on clock differences that stores a convex clock zone. Its canonical form is all-pairs shortest paths, computed by Floyd-Warshall in O(n^3).

name: Cross-entropy loss
summary: The negative log probability that a categorical model gives the true label. It is cross-entropy against the one-hot label, and its gradient in the logits is p - y.

name: Mex function
summary: Function giving the smallest nonnegative integer missing from a set, used to compute Grundy values of game positions.

name: Bitstate hashing
summary: Store the visited set of an explicit-state search as k bits per state in a large bit array, like a Bloom filter, so that far larger state spaces fit in memory at the price of skipping some states.

name: Layer normalization
summary: Normalize the features of one example with their own mean and variance, then apply a learned scale and shift. It needs no batch statistics, so training and inference agree.

name: Slitherlink problem
summary: Draw a single loop satisfying the clue counts around cells; NP-complete.

name: Incremental PCA
aliases: sequential Karhunen-Loeve algorithm with mean update
summary: Update a thin SVD of the centered data batch by batch, with a correction column for the moving mean, so PCA never holds all the data. Exact when no rank is truncated.

name: Mean-field approximation
summary: Fit a fully factorized q to a Markov random field by coordinate ascent. Each update raises a lower bound on log Z. q seeks one mode, since it minimizes KL(q || p).

name: Clustering feature tree
summary: Height-balanced tree whose nodes store clustering-feature summaries, used by BIRCH.

name: String constraint satisfiability
summary: Decide constraints over string concatenation, length and regular-language membership.

name: Sussman anomaly
summary: Goal interactions in blocks world that defeat naive linear, goal-by-goal planners.

name: Hinge loss
summary: The margin loss max(0, 1 - y f) of support vector machines. It is convex, has a subgradient, and its conditional risk is minimized by sign(2 eta - 1).

name: Ancestral sampling
summary: Draw an exact sample from the joint distribution of a Bayesian network: draw each variable from its CPT, parents before children.

name: Sauer-Shelah lemma
summary: A class of VC dimension d realizes at most sum over i <= d of C(n, i) <= (en/d)^d labelings of n points, so its growth is polynomial in n, not exponential.

name: Maintaining arc consistency
summary: Backtracking search for a binary CSP that makes the unassigned variables arc consistent after each assignment, and backtracks when a domain becomes empty.

name: HTN planning
summary: Find a primitive plan obtained by decomposing a given initial task network.

name: Counting constraint satisfaction problem
summary: Count the number of satisfying assignments of a constraint problem.

name: Ensemble learning
summary: Train several predictors and combine them by vote, average or a learned rule. The combination helps when the members are accurate and make different errors.

name: Junction tree
aliases: junction tree of a triangulated graph
summary: A tree whose nodes are the maximal cliques of a triangulated graph, in which the cliques that hold any one vertex form a connected subtree.

name: Boosting
summary: Train weak learners one after another, each on data reweighted or relabeled to fix the errors of the sum so far, and combine them by a weighted vote or sum.

name: Davis-Putnam procedure
summary: Decide SAT with no search. Apply the unit and pure literal rules, and remove one variable at a time by replacing its clauses with all their resolvents on it.

name: SLD resolution
summary: Goal-directed resolution for definite programs. Each step picks an atom of the goal, unifies it with a clause head and puts the body in its place. It is sound and complete for any choice rule.

name: Model-based reinforcement learning
summary: Learn the transition probabilities and rewards from experience, then plan on the learned model. Errors in the model limit the quality of the plan.

name: Boolean quantifier elimination
summary: Remove quantified variables from a boolean formula to obtain an equivalent quantifier-free function.

name: Iterative-deepening A*
summary: Depth-first search with an f-cost bound that increases each iteration; linear memory, optimal with admissible h.

name: Modified policy iteration
summary: Each iteration takes a greedy policy and then evaluates it only partially, with m backups. Order m = 0 is value iteration and m = infinity is policy iteration.

name: Cross-validation
summary: Estimate the risk of a learning procedure by partitioning the data into K folds, training on K - 1 of them, testing on the rest, and averaging over the folds.

name: Linear-time complexity of CTL model checking
aliases: CTL model checking in linear time
summary: CTL model checking takes time O(|M||phi|), linear in the structure and in the formula. EG costs linear time through strongly connected components, and fairness keeps the bound polynomial.

name: Algebraic decision diagram
summary: A reduced ordered BDD whose sinks hold values from any set, such as numbers. It represents functions from bit vectors to values canonically and combines them with any pointwise operation.

name: Conditional random field
summary: A discriminative undirected model of P(labels | observations). A linear-chain CRF is trained by a concave likelihood and decoded by Viterbi in O(n k^2).

name: Decidability of Petri net reachability
summary: Whether a Petri net can reach a given marking exactly is decidable (Mayr 1981, Kosaraju 1982). The problem is Ackermann-complete.

name: Dasgupta's cost
summary: A cost of a hierarchy on a similarity graph: each edge ij pays w_ij times the number of leaves below the lowest common ancestor of i and j.

name: Elbow method
aliases: elbow criterion for the number of clusters
summary: Plot the within-cluster sum of squares W_k against k and choose k at the bend. It is a heuristic; the bend has no single definition, and rules such as the chord rule are one choice of many.

name: Precision and recall
summary: Precision TP/(TP+FP) and recall TP/(TP+FN), their F-beta mean, micro, macro and weighted averages, and the precision-recall curve with average precision.

name: Game tree evaluation
summary: Compute the minimax value of the root of a given game tree.

name: Theta*
summary: Any-angle path planning on grids using line-of-sight shortcuts within A*.

name: Two watched literals
summary: Watch two literals of each clause, and look at a clause only when one of its watches becomes false. Unit propagation then touches few clauses and needs no work on backtrack.

name: Unit propagation
summary: Repeatedly assign the literal forced by a unit clause until no clause is unit or some clause is false. The main inference step of DPLL and CDCL.

name: Bagging
summary: Fit one learner on many bootstrap resamples of the data and average or vote. It lowers the variance of unstable learners, and the left-out examples give a free error estimate.

name: Intrinsic dimension estimation
summary: Estimate the intrinsic dimension of a point cloud from local geometry or nearest-neighbour statistics.

name: Generalized advantage estimation
summary: Advantage estimate A_t = sum_l (gamma lambda)^l delta_(t+l) from TD errors of a critic; lambda = 0 gives the TD error, lambda = 1 the return minus V.

name: Transposition table
summary: Hash table caching search results for positions reached by different move orders.

name: Generalized geography
summary: Two-player game on a directed graph, shown PSPACE-complete by Lichtenstein and Sipser.

name: Skolemization
summary: Replace each existential quantifier by a new function of the universal variables around it. The result is satisfiable exactly when the input is, but it is not equivalent to it.

name: First-order theorem proving
summary: Decide whether a first-order sentence follows from given axioms. It is semi-decidable, by Herbrand's theorem or resolution, and undecidable (Church 1936, Turing 1936).

name: Ridge regression
summary: Least squares with a penalty λ||w||^2. Solve (X^T X + λI) w = X^T y on centered data; each singular direction shrinks by σ^2/(σ^2 + λ).

name: Huet's pre-unification
summary: A semi-decision procedure for higher-order unification. It guesses heads by imitation or projection and stops when only flex-flex pairs are left, so it finds a complete set of pre-unifiers.

name: Symmetry reduction
summary: Explore one representative state per orbit of a symmetry group of the system. The quotient is bisimilar to the system, so symmetric properties are preserved.

name: Learning rate schedule
summary: A rule that sets the step size of each optimizer step during training, such as step decay, cosine annealing, linear warmup, one cycle or inverse square root.

name: Dendrogram
summary: Rooted binary tree of a hierarchical clustering: each internal node merges two clusters and is drawn at the height of that merge.

name: k-means clustering problem
summary: Choose k centers in R^d that minimize the sum of squared Euclidean distances from each point to its nearest center.

name: Unsatisfiable core
summary: A subset of the assertions of an unsatisfiable problem that is still unsatisfiable. Solvers need not return a minimal one; a minimal unsatisfiable subset is a core with no smaller core inside.

name: Canonical correlation analysis
summary: Find paired directions a and b for two sets of variables that maximize corr(a^T x, b^T y). The answer is the SVD of C_XX^(-1/2) C_XY C_YY^(-1/2).

name: Implication graph
summary: Directed acyclic graph of the assignments of a SAT search. Each forced literal has edges from the literals that forced it. CDCL reads its conflict clauses and UIPs from it.

name: Parallel portfolio solving
summary: Run several differently configured CDCL solvers on the same formula in parallel, share short learned clauses, and return the first answer.

name: RRT-Connect
summary: Grows two RRTs from start and goal and extends each greedily toward the other.

name: Markov property
summary: The rules that read conditional independences off a graph: pairwise, local and global for undirected graphs, and the local directed property for DAGs.

name: Stacking
summary: Fit a level-1 learner on the out-of-fold predictions of several level-0 learners. In-sample predictions leak the labels and give an over-optimistic combination.

name: Relaxation heuristic
summary: Derives an admissible heuristic by solving a problem with some constraints removed.

name: Beam-stack search
summary: Beam search with a stack that allows backtracking to recover from beam pruning.

name: Actor-critic
summary: Policy gradient where a learned critic V_w supplies the TD error delta = R + gamma V_w(S') - V_w(S), which replaces the Monte Carlo return in the update of the actor pi_theta.

name: On-the-fly model checking
summary: Generate the product of the system and the property automaton only as the search needs it, and stop at the first violation, so that an error can be found before the state space is built.

name: Complemented edges
summary: Store negation on edges so that f and its complement share one node, roughly halving size.

name: Substitution
summary: A map from variables to terms that changes only finitely many variables, applied to a term by replacing each variable at the same time.

name: Modal mu-calculus
summary: Modal logic with least and greatest fixed-point operators. It contains CTL, LTL and CTL*, it cannot tell bisimilar states apart, and its model checking is equivalent to solving parity games.

name: Least commitment principle
summary: Postpone ordering and variable-binding decisions until they are forced.

name: Forward checking
summary: Backtracking search for a binary CSP that, after each assignment, removes the conflicting values from the domains of the unassigned neighbours and backtracks when a domain becomes empty.

name: Halfspace learning
summary: Learn a classifier sign(w . x + b) from labeled points. Consistent learning is a linear program, solvable in polynomial time; agnostic learning is NP-hard.

name: Interval constraint propagation
summary: Narrows the interval domains of real variables by revising one constraint at a time with interval arithmetic. HC4 revises a constraint by a forward and a backward pass over its tree.

name: Kinodynamic planning
summary: Motion planning subject to dynamics and velocity or acceleration constraints.

name: Heuristic function
summary: A function h(n) estimating the cost of the cheapest path from a state n to a goal.

name: Opening book
summary: Precomputed table mapping opening positions to recommended moves.

name: Frame problem
summary: Specifying which facts an action leaves unchanged, without listing every non-effect.

name: Adafactor
summary: An adaptive optimizer that stores the second moment of an n by m weight matrix as row and column sums, O(n + m) memory, with update clipping and relative step sizes.

name: Pushdown system
summary: A finite control with an unbounded stack and no input. It models programs with recursion; its infinite configuration graph still has regular reachability sets.

name: Naive Bayes classifier
summary: A generative classifier that assumes the features are independent given the class. It counts in one pass and predicts with argmax of log P(c) + Σ log P(x_j | c).

name: Causal link
summary: A commitment that one step produces a precondition of a later step; other steps may threaten it.

name: BIRCH
aliases: balanced iterative reducing and clustering using hierarchies
summary: Single-pass clustering that summarises points in a clustering-feature tree.

name: Backbone of a formula
summary: The literals that are true in every model of a satisfiable formula; testing one literal is coNP-complete, and the whole backbone needs at most n + 1 SAT calls.

name: BDD variable ordering problem
summary: Find the variable order with the smallest reduced ordered BDD. The size can change by an exponential factor with the order, and the decision version is NP-complete.

name: Overfitting
summary: A learned model fits its training examples, noise included, much better than new data, so its training error is low and its true error is high. A validation set detects it.

name: Rademacher complexity
summary: How well a function class correlates with random signs on the sample. Twice it, plus a confidence term, bounds the generalization gap of every function in the class.

name: Normalized mutual information
aliases: normalized mutual information of two clusterings
summary: The mutual information of two partitions divided by a mean of their entropies, so it lies in [0, 1]. It is not corrected for chance; the adjusted mutual information is.

name: Boolean constraint satisfaction problem
summary: CSP in which every variable is Boolean and the constraints come from a fixed relation set.

name: Forward state-space search (progression)
summary: Searches from the initial state, applying applicable actions until the goal holds.

name: SAT-based bounded model checking
summary: Unroll the transition relation k times into one formula, add the negated property (with a loop condition for liveness), convert to CNF and ask a SAT solver; a model is a counterexample.

name: Support vector machine
summary: A linear or kernel classifier that maximizes the margin 2/||w|| between the classes, with slack weighted by C. Trained by solving a convex dual QP; only the support vectors matter.

name: Generalization error
summary: The expected loss L_D(h) of a hypothesis on new examples from the data distribution, and its gap to the training error. Hoeffding bounds the gap for a fixed h, not for a learned one.

name: ID3 algorithm
summary: Quinlan's 1986 tree learner for categorical attributes: split each node on the attribute of largest information gain, one branch per value, until the nodes are pure.

name: G-means
summary: Increases k until every cluster passes a Gaussianity test.

name: Gradient checking
summary: Test an analytic gradient by comparing each entry with a central difference (f(t + h e_i) - f(t - h e_i)) / 2h, using a relative error.

name: Canopy clustering
aliases: canopy clustering of McCallum, Nigam and Ungar
summary: Cheap overlapping pre-clustering used to limit the expensive distance computations of a later clustering step.

name: Backward state-space search (regression)
summary: Searches backward from the goal, regressing subgoals through relevant actions.

name: Batch normalization
summary: Normalize each feature of a layer with the mean and variance of the current mini-batch, then apply a learned scale and shift. Inference uses running averages of the statistics.

name: Black-box variational inference
summary: Stochastic gradient ascent on the ELBO with Monte Carlo score function gradients, made usable by Rao-Blackwellization and control variates. It needs only samples from q and values of log p.

name: Most general unifier
summary: A unifier of which every other unifier is an instance; unique up to variable renaming.

name: Locality preserving projections
summary: A linear form of Laplacian eigenmaps: find the projection directions a that solve X L Xᵀ a = λ X D Xᵀ a, so neighbors stay close and new points have a map.

name: Kernel trick
summary: Write a linear method so that the data enter only through inner products, then replace each inner product by a PSD kernel k(x, z) = φ(x)·φ(z) without forming φ.

name: Search extensions
summary: Searches certain forcing lines, such as checks, one ply deeper than the nominal depth.

name: Kociemba's two-phase algorithm
summary: Two-phase search that reduces the cube to a subgroup and then solves it, giving near-optimal solutions.

name: Biclustering problem
summary: Find submatrices of a data matrix (a subset of rows with a subset of columns) whose entries follow a pattern, such as a low mean squared residue. NP-hard in its main forms.

name: Principal component analysis
summary: Project centered data onto the k orthogonal directions of largest variance: the top eigenvectors of the covariance matrix, or the top right singular vectors of the data.

name: Hyperparameter tuning
summary: Choose the settings fixed before training, such as the learning rate, to minimize validation loss. An expensive noisy black box; solved by grid, random search, successive halving, Hyperband.

name: Reduced ordered binary decision diagram
summary: An OBDD with no redundant tests and no duplicate nodes; canonical for a fixed order.

name: Bisimulation
summary: A relation between states such that related states match each other's transitions into related states; bisimilarity, the largest one, is the greatest fixed point of this condition.

name: Deadly triad
summary: Function approximation, bootstrapping and off-policy training together can make TD value estimates diverge. Any two of the three are safe in the linear case.

name: Stochastic shortest path problem
summary: Find a policy minimizing expected total cost to reach a goal in an MDP.

name: Shostak's combination method
summary: Decides equalities in a theory with a canonizer and a solver, such as linear arithmetic, together with uninterpreted functions, by keeping one solved form instead of exchanging equalities.

name: Bisecting k-means
summary: A divisive heuristic for k-means: start with one cluster and repeatedly split the largest one, or the one with the largest SSE, by 2-means.

name: Information gain
summary: The drop in label entropy from splitting a set of examples: IG = H(Y) - H(Y | split). ID3 and C4.5 choose the split of largest gain or gain ratio.

name: Partition function computation
summary: Compute Z, the sum of a product of factors over all configurations. Elimination takes time exponential in the induced width; in general it is #P-hard.

name: Optimal efficiency of A*
summary: No algorithm using the same heuristic expands fewer nodes than A* without missing needed nodes.

name: Minimax algorithm
summary: Evaluates a game tree by maximizing at the mover's nodes and minimizing at the opponent's nodes.

name: Linear resolution
summary: Resolution in one chain, where each new clause comes from the last one and an input clause or an earlier clause of the chain. Refutation complete (Loveland 1970, Luckham 1970).

name: Game tree
summary: Rooted tree whose nodes are game positions and whose edges are legal moves; leaves are terminal positions.

name: Cluster purity
summary: The share of objects that are in the majority class of their cluster. It is 1 for singleton clusters, so it cannot compare clusterings with different numbers of clusters.

name: Don't-care-based function minimization
summary: Given BDDs of f and a care set c, find the smallest BDD of a g that equals f wherever c is 1. The problem is NP-complete even for a fixed order, so tools use heuristics.

name: RRT*
summary: RRT variant that rewires the tree to converge toward optimal paths.

name: Gaussian mixture model
summary: Probabilistic clustering model in which the data come from a mixture of Gaussian components.

name: Lazy abstraction with interpolants
summary: Unwind a program into an abstract reachability tree, and on a spurious error path add interpolant predicates only at its locations and rebuild only the affected subtree.

name: Move ordering
summary: Heuristic order of trying moves so that alpha-beta cuts off as early as possible.

name: Robust PCA
summary: Split a data matrix into a low-rank part and a sparse part of gross errors by minimizing the nuclear norm plus lambda times the l1 norm, solved with an augmented Lagrangian method.

name: k-nearest neighbors
summary: Predict the label of a query by a vote of its k closest training points, or its value by their mean. No training step; Θ(n d) work per query by brute force.

name: Petri net
summary: A bipartite graph of places and transitions in which tokens move when transitions fire. It models concurrent systems with unbounded counters but no zero tests.

name: Multidimensional scaling
summary: Place n points in a low dimension so that their distances fit given dissimilarities: in value (metric MDS) or only in rank order (Kruskal's nonmetric MDS).

name: Margin-based generalization bound
summary: A linear classifier of norm 1 on data of norm at most R has error at most its fraction of margin below gamma plus about 2R/(gamma sqrt(n)), with no dependence on the dimension.

name: Decision tree
summary: A rooted tree that predicts. Each internal node tests one feature, each leaf holds a label or a value, and a prediction follows one root-to-leaf path in O(depth) tests.

name: Partitioning around medoids
summary: Local search that swaps medoids with non-medoid points while the total dissimilarity decreases.

name: Hypothesis class
summary: The set H of functions from inputs to labels that a learner may output. Its choice before the data is seen is the inductive bias, and its size or VC dimension sets the data a learner needs.

name: Dual encoding
summary: Transforms a CSP with non-binary constraints into an equivalent binary CSP by making each constraint a variable.

name: SARSA
summary: On-policy TD control: after each step, move Q(S,A) toward R + gamma Q(S',A'), where A' is the next action the epsilon-greedy policy really takes.

name: Early stopping
summary: Stop training when the error on held-out data stops improving, and keep the best parameters seen. For gradient descent on least squares it acts like ridge regression.

name: One-vs-rest
summary: Reduce k-class classification to k binary problems, class j against all others, and predict the class whose binary score is largest.

name: Policy gradient theorem
aliases: policy gradient theorem of Sutton et al.
summary: The gradient of the expected return of a policy pi_theta is sum_s d(s) sum_a grad pi(a | s) Q(s, a), with d the discounted state visits. It needs no derivative of the state distribution.

name: XGBoost
summary: Gradient tree boosting with a second-order objective, leaf weights -G/(H + λ), a split gain with penalties λ and γ, default directions for missing values and a weighted quantile sketch.

name: Probabilistic CTL
summary: CTL with the path quantifiers replaced by a probability operator P⋈p, interpreted over Markov chains, plus a step-bounded until. Defined by Hansson and Jonsson in 1994.

name: BDD apply algorithm
summary: Combines two BDDs with a binary boolean operator in time proportional to the product of their sizes.

name: Cluster validity
summary: How to judge a clustering: external indices compare it with known classes, internal indices use only the data, and relative criteria compare clusterings, for example to choose k.

name: Belief propagation
summary: Exact marginals on a tree-shaped factor graph by sum-product messages: one pass to a root and one back, two messages per edge.

name: Zermelo's theorem
summary: Every finite perfect-information two-player zero-sum game has a value achieved by optimal pure strategies.

name: Importance sampling for off-policy learning
summary: Reweight returns from a behavior policy mu by products of ratios pi/mu to estimate values of a target policy pi. Ordinary IS is unbiased; weighted IS is biased with lower variance.

name: Latin square completion
summary: Complete a partial Latin square; NP-complete in general.

name: E-matching
summary: Finds all ways to make a pattern with variables equal to a term in an e-graph, modulo its ground equalities. SMT solvers use the matches to instantiate quantified formulas.

name: Binary resolution rule
summary: The inference rule that takes two clauses, renames them apart, unifies one literal of each with a complementary one by an mgu, and adds the resolvent. With factoring it is refutation complete.

name: Symbolic reachability analysis
summary: Compute the set of reachable states as a least fixed point of image steps, where each set of states and the transition relation are BDDs and each image is one relational product.

name: Nash equilibrium
summary: Strategy profile in which no player can improve their payoff by unilaterally changing strategy.

name: Smoothing
summary: Compute p(x_t | y_1..T), the distribution of a past hidden state of a state-space model given observations before and after it. Fixed-interval, fixed-lag and fixed-point.

name: Urban-Pitts-Gabbay nominal unification
summary: Transformation rules for nominal unification. Equations are simplified first, then freshness problems. The result is a most general solution, a substitution with freshness constraints.

name: Deep Q-network
summary: Q-learning with a neural network Q(s, a; theta), trained by SGD on minibatches from a replay buffer against targets from a target network that is copied every C steps. No convergence guarantee.

name: SLINK
summary: Sibson's single linkage algorithm: adds one point at a time to a pointer form (pi, lambda) of the tree, in O(n^2) time and O(n) memory.

name: Sudoku problem
summary: Fill a partially given grid so each row, column and box has all symbols; generalized to n-by-n is NP-complete.

name: Correlation clustering
summary: Given a + or - label on each pair of items, partition the items to minimize disagreements (+ pairs split, - pairs joined). The number of clusters is free. NP-hard.

name: Nearest-neighbor chain algorithm
summary: Agglomerative clustering that follows nearest neighbors until two clusters are mutual nearest neighbors, then merges them: O(n^2) for reducible linkages.

name: Generative versus discriminative models
summary: A generative model fits the joint p(x, y) and classifies by Bayes' rule; a discriminative model fits p(y | x) or the boundary directly. Each wins in a different regime.

name: HMM evaluation
summary: Compute P(O | model), the probability that a hidden Markov model emits a given observation sequence. A direct sum has N^T terms; the forward algorithm takes O(T N^2).

name: t-SNE
summary: Symmetric SNE with a Student t kernel of one degree of freedom in the map, which relieves crowding; fitted by gradient descent, mainly to draw 2D maps of data.

name: Equivalent literal substitution
summary: Find literals that must be equal by computing the strongly connected components of the binary implication graph, and replace each component by one representative literal.

name: Inverse reinforcement learning
summary: Find a reward function for which observed expert behavior is optimal or most likely. The answer is never unique: the zero reward explains every policy, so methods add a criterion.

name: Tree-reweighted belief propagation
summary: Message passing with edge weights from a distribution over spanning trees. It maximizes a concave function on the local polytope whose maximum is an upper bound on log Z.

name: Gaussian belief propagation
summary: Belief propagation for a Gaussian graphical model in information form. Exact on trees; on graphs with cycles, if it converges the means are exact but the variances are not.

name: Variational inference
summary: Approximate a posterior p(z | x) by the member of a tractable family Q that maximizes the ELBO, which is the same as to minimize KL(q || p(z | x)).

name: Bayes optimal classifier
summary: The rule that predicts the label with the largest posterior P(y | x). It has the smallest possible 0-1 risk, the Bayes risk; a loss matrix gives the cost-sensitive version.

name: Gaussian graphical model
summary: A multivariate normal distribution with a graph: an edge is missing exactly when the precision matrix has a zero there, which means conditional independence given the rest.

name: Bit-blasting
summary: Encode bit-vector operations as Boolean circuits so a SAT solver can decide them.

name: Lottery ticket hypothesis
summary: The empirical claim that a random dense network holds a sparse subnetwork that, reset to its initial weights, trains to the same accuracy. Found by iterative magnitude pruning.

name: Complete-linkage clustering
summary: Agglomerative clustering that merges the two clusters whose farthest pair of points is closest. Each merge height is the diameter of the new cluster.

name: Reinforcement learning control
aliases: learning an optimal policy from interaction
summary: Find a good policy for an MDP whose transitions and rewards are unknown, using only sampled experience. The main solver families are value based, policy based and model based.

name: Model-based theory combination
summary: Each theory solver keeps a candidate model. Equalities between shared terms that hold in a model are tried as decisions, and the formula is satisfiable when all models agree.

name: Tseitin transformation
summary: Convert a Boolean circuit into an equisatisfiable CNF of linear size, with one new variable for each gate.

name: Nurikabe problem
summary: Shade cells to form one connected sea around numbered islands; NP-complete.

name: CART
summary: Breiman et al. 1984: grow a large binary tree by Gini or squared-error decrease, with surrogate splits, then prune it by cost-complexity with alpha chosen by cross-validation.

name: Temporal-difference error
summary: The TD error is R_(t+1) + gamma V(S_(t+1)) - V(S_t). Its mean is the Bellman residual, and with V fixed the discounted TD errors of an episode sum to G_t - V(S_t).

name: Warnsdorff's rule
summary: Greedy heuristic that always moves the knight to the square with the fewest onward moves.

name: Gaussian process
summary: A distribution over functions in which every finite set of values is jointly Gaussian; GP regression gives a closed form posterior in O(n^3) time by Cholesky.

name: FastICA
summary: A fixed-point ICA method: after whitening, w ← E[z g(wᵀz)] − E[g'(wᵀz)] w, then normalize. It converges cubically with the kurtosis nonlinearity and needs no step size.

name: A* search
summary: Best-first search ordering nodes by f = g + h; optimal when h is admissible.

name: Mean squared error
summary: The mean of the squared differences between predictions and targets. Its minimizer is the conditional mean, and for an estimator it splits into variance plus squared bias.

name: Polyomino tiling problem
summary: Decide whether a region can be exactly covered by copies of given polyominoes; NP-complete in general.

name: Conjugate prior
summary: A family of priors that a likelihood maps to posteriors in the same family, so Bayesian updating only changes a few hyperparameters. Every exponential family has one.

name: XOR-SAT
summary: SAT where each clause is an XOR of variables with a fixed parity. It is a linear system over GF(2), so Gaussian elimination decides it and counts its models in polynomial time.

name: Label smoothing
summary: Train a classifier on the target (1 - ε) y + ε/K instead of the one-hot label y. This adds ε times a cross-entropy to the uniform distribution and keeps the logits bounded.

name: Theory of arrays satisfiability
summary: Decide formulas with select and store operations over array variables.

name: Affinity propagation
summary: Points exchange responsibility and availability messages (max-sum on a factor graph) until a set of exemplars emerges. No convergence or optimality guarantee.

name: Potential field method
summary: Follows the gradient of attractive goal and repulsive obstacle potentials; can trap in local minima.

name: Blind source separation
summary: Recover source signals s(t) from mixtures x(t) = A s(t) when both the sources and the mixing matrix A are unknown. The answer is defined only up to order and scale.

name: Miller pattern unification
summary: Compute a most general unifier of two higher-order patterns, or report that there is none. Each step is forced, so there is no search, and Qian's version runs in linear time.

name: Herbrand universe
summary: The set of ground terms built from the constants and function symbols of a clause set. A clause set has a model if and only if it has one whose domain is this set, with each term naming itself.

name: Message passing
summary: Compute a global sum of products by local messages on a graph. On a tree, each edge carries one message each way, and the operations can be any commutative semiring.

name: Expectation propagation
aliases: expectation propagation for approximate Bayesian inference
summary: Approximates each factor of a posterior by an exponential family site, refined one at a time by moment matching against the true factor times the rest. Mass covering; no convergence guarantee.

name: Least-squares temporal-difference learning
summary: Estimate the matrix A and vector b of linear TD from a batch of transitions and solve A theta = b directly. No step size; O(d^2) per step with Sherman-Morrison updates.

name: Gradient checkpointing
summary: Keep only some activations in the forward pass and recompute the rest in the backward pass: O(sqrt n) memory for one extra forward pass on an n-layer chain.

name: Horn-SAT
summary: SAT where each clause has at most one positive literal. Solvable in linear time by forward chaining, and a satisfiable instance has a least model.

name: Semidefinite embedding
summary: Find the centered Gram matrix of largest trace that keeps all distances between neighbors, a semidefinite program, then embed with its top eigenvectors as in classical MDS.

name: Interpolation-based model checking
summary: Prove an invariant by growing an over-approximate reachable set with Craig interpolants taken from unsatisfiable BMC queries, and increasing the depth after a spurious hit.

name: Minimum description length
summary: Choose the model that gives the shortest code for the data: the bits to describe the model plus the bits to describe the data with the help of the model.

name: Rush Hour problem
summary: Slide vehicles to free a target car from a traffic grid; PSPACE-complete for the generalized version.

name: Monte Carlo tree search
summary: Builds a search tree with random playouts, selecting nodes by a bandit-style rule and backing up results.

name: Zero-suppressed binary decision diagram
summary: An ordered decision diagram that removes nodes whose high edge goes to the empty family. It stores families of sets canonically and is small for sparse families.

name: Equational unification
summary: Find substitutions that make two terms equal modulo a set of equations, and classify theories by the shape of their solution sets.

name: Compositional verification
summary: Verify a parallel composition by checking each component, or a small abstraction of it, and combining the results by a sound rule, so that the full product is never built.

name: Maximum constraint satisfaction problem
summary: Find an assignment that satisfies the largest number of constraints, or the largest total weight. It is NP-hard even for two values and binary constraints, and exact solvers use branch and bound.

name: Simulation relation
summary: A relation in which the second state can match every step of the first, in one direction only; the simulation preorder preserves universal temporal properties such as ACTL*.

name: Softmax regression
summary: Logistic regression for K classes. P(y = k | x) is the softmax of K linear scores, fit by minimizing cross-entropy, with gradient X^T(P - Y)/n.

name: Hard and soft clustering
summary: Hard clustering assigns each point to one cluster; soft clustering gives each point membership degrees.

name: Linear separability
summary: Two labelled point sets are linearly separable when a hyperplane has all positive points strictly on one side and all negative points strictly on the other.

name: Exploding gradient problem
summary: The backpropagated gradient can grow exponentially with depth or sequence length when the Jacobians it passes through expand, as when a recurrent weight matrix has spectral radius above 1.

name: Non-chronological backtracking
summary: After a conflict, undo every decision level above the second highest level of the learned clause, possibly many, and assert the clause's one literal of the conflict level there.

name: Backdoor criterion
summary: If Z has no descendant of X and blocks every path into X, then P(y | do(x)) is the sum over z of P(y | x, z) P(z), so the effect follows from observational data.

name: Partial-order planning (POP)
summary: Refines partial plans by resolving open preconditions and causal-link threats.

name: Factor analysis
summary: A latent Gaussian model x = mu + Lambda z + eps with a diagonal noise covariance Psi. Fitted by maximum likelihood with EM; the loadings are only defined up to a rotation.

name: Undecidability of semi-unification
summary: Semi-unification is undecidable, proved by Kfoury, Tiuryn and Urzyczyn with a reduction from Turing machine boundedness; so type inference with polymorphic recursion is undecidable.

name: h-max heuristic
summary: Admissible planning heuristic taking the maximum cost over precondition facts.

name: Gittins index
summary: Give each arm in each state the best discounted reward per unit of discounted time it can earn before a stopping time. Pulling the arm with the largest index is optimal.

name: Backpropagation
summary: Compute the gradient of a network's loss for all weights in one backward sweep, by the delta recursion delta_l = (W_(l+1)^T delta_(l+1)) * f'(z_l).

name: Incremental solving
summary: Solve a sequence of related queries with one solver, adding and removing assertions with push and pop, or passing temporary assumptions, so that learned facts carry over between the queries.

name: Davies-Bouldin index
summary: The mean over clusters of the worst ratio (S_i + S_j)/M_ij of spread to centroid distance. Lower is better. This page uses q = 1 and p = 2.

name: Markov blanket
summary: A set of variables that makes one variable independent of all the others. In a Bayesian network: parents, children, co-parents. In a Markov random field: neighbours.

name: PCTL model checking
summary: Decide which states of a finite Markov chain satisfy a PCTL formula. Graph search plus one linear system per until gives time polynomial in the chain and linear in the formula.

name: Conflict-directed backjumping
summary: Backtracking that records, for each variable, the earlier variables that made its values fail, and at a dead end jumps back to the latest of them, merging the sets so that no solution is skipped.

name: Invariant checking
summary: Decide whether a state predicate holds in every reachable state, and give a path to a bad state when it does not. It is reachability of the complement, the simplest safety check.

name: 2-SAT algorithm
summary: Solve 2-SAT in linear time. Find the strongly connected components of the implication graph; UNSAT when a variable and its negation share one, else read a model from their order.

name: Generalized belief propagation
summary: Message passing between regions (clusters of variables) of a region graph. Its fixed points are the stationary points of the Kikuchi free energy, which generalizes the Bethe one.

name: Cube-and-conquer
summary: Split the formula into many cubes with a lookahead solver that cuts its tree by a dynamic threshold, then solve each cube with incremental CDCL under assumptions.

name: Temporal logic
summary: Logics that express how a system behaves over time, with operators such as always, eventually and until. LTL is linear, CTL is branching, CTL* holds both, and the mu-calculus holds all three.

name: Window permutation reordering
summary: A BDD reordering heuristic. It tries all orders of each window of w adjacent levels by adjacent swaps, keeps the best order of the window, and repeats until no window improves the size.

name: Perceptron
summary: Online learner for a linear classifier. On each mistake it adds y times x to the weights. On separable data it stops after at most (R/γ)^2 mistakes.

name: Pivot algorithm for correlation clustering
summary: Pick a random pivot, cluster it with its + neighbors, remove them, repeat. An expected 3-approximation for correlation clustering on complete graphs (Ailon, Charikar, Newman).

name: Prenex normal form
summary: A first-order formula with all its quantifiers in a prefix at the front and a quantifier-free matrix after them. Every formula has an equivalent prenex form.

name: Horizon effect
summary: Error where a depth-limited search misjudges a position because a consequence lies beyond the horizon.

name: Global constraint
aliases: n-ary constraint with a dedicated propagator
summary: A constraint over any number of variables, such as all-different or cumulative, with its own propagator. The propagator removes values that its decomposition into small constraints keeps.

name: Weighted A*
summary: A* with f = g + w*h for w > 1, trading solution bound for speed.

name: Equality with uninterpreted functions (EUF) satisfiability
summary: Decide whether a quantifier-free formula of equalities between terms built from free function symbols has a model. Conjunctions take O(n log n) time; with Boolean structure it is NP-complete.

name: Weight normalization
summary: Write each weight vector as w = g v/||v||, a learned length g times a learned direction, and train g and v. The gradient in v is orthogonal to v.

name: Tarski's decidability theorem
aliases: quantifier elimination for real closed fields
summary: The first-order theory of real closed fields, including real arithmetic, is decidable.

name: Sliding tile puzzle
summary: Slide numbered tiles into the blank space to reach a goal arrangement.

name: Undecidability of higher-order unification
summary: No algorithm decides whether two simply typed λ-terms with third-order variables have a unifier. Huet and Lucchesi proved it in 1972 and 1973 by reduction from Post's correspondence problem.

name: SMACOF
aliases: scaling by majorizing a complicated function
summary: Minimize the raw stress of metric MDS by majorization: repeat the Guttman transform X = (1/n) B(X) X. The stress never increases.

name: Parallel alpha-beta search
summary: Alpha-beta parallelized across processors by searching eldest children first, then the rest in parallel.

name: Macro-operators
summary: Precomputed action sequences added as single operators to shorten plans and search.

name: Local tangent space alignment
summary: Find local PCA tangent coordinates in each neighborhood, then find global coordinates that are an affine image of each local set, from the bottom eigenvectors of an alignment matrix.

name: BDD quantification
summary: Computes exists x. f and forall x. f as f|x=0 OR f|x=1 and AND.

name: k-SAT
summary: SAT restricted to clauses of at most k literals. Linear for k = 2 and NP-complete for k >= 3; the best known algorithms take 2^((1 - c/k)n) time, and ETH and SETH say how far this can improve.

name: Hierarchical task network
summary: Formalism in which tasks are recursively decomposed into subtasks and primitive actions.

name: Superposition
summary: Paramodulation restricted by a reduction ordering, with equality resolution, equality factoring and deletion of redundant clauses. Refutation complete for equality (Bachmair and Ganzinger 1990).

name: Expectiminimax
summary: Minimax extended with chance nodes whose value is the expected value over outcomes.

name: Neural network pruning
summary: Remove weights, neurons or channels that matter least for the loss, then fine-tune. Scores range from the weight magnitude to the second order saliencies of optimal brain damage and surgeon.

name: Omega test
summary: Decision procedure for integer linear arithmetic built on Fourier-Motzkin with exact integer shadows.

name: Phase saving
summary: When a backtrack unassigns a variable, store its value; when the solver later decides that variable, give it the stored value. Backjumps and restarts then lose less work.

name: Safety property
summary: A property stating that nothing bad happens. Each violation has a finite bad prefix, and the safety properties are exactly the closed sets of infinite words.

name: Maximum likelihood estimation
summary: Pick the parameter that gives the observed data the highest probability. Invariant, consistent and efficient in regular models; fails in Neyman-Scott and mixtures.

name: Kernel k-means
summary: K-means carried out in the feature space of a kernel, using only the kernel matrix; its weighted form is equivalent to normalized cut.

name: TD(lambda)
summary: Learn V toward the lambda-return, a geometric mix of n-step returns. Traces give the same total update offline, step by step, without waiting for the end.

name: Perceptron convergence theorem
summary: If each example has norm at most R and a unit vector separates them with margin γ, the perceptron makes at most (R/γ)^2 mistakes, in any order.

name: Dropout
summary: During training, keep each unit with probability p and scale the kept units by 1/p, so test time needs no change. For linear regression it equals an adaptive L2 penalty.

name: Convex theory
summary: A theory in which a set of literals that entails a disjunction of equalities between constants already entails one of them. In combination, convex theories only need to exchange single equalities.

name: Path consistency
summary: Every consistent assignment to a pair of variables extends to any third variable along each path of the constraint graph.

name: Proof-number search
summary: Best-first search on AND/OR trees that tracks proof and disproof numbers to prove a win or loss.

name: Ordered binary decision diagram
summary: A BDD in which every path tests variables in one fixed global order.

name: Calinski-Harabasz index
summary: The ratio [tr(B)/(k-1)] / [tr(W)/(n-k)] of between-cluster to within-cluster scatter for points in R^d. Higher is better; it is the F statistic of a one-way ANOVA.

name: SAS+ finite-domain representation
summary: State variables with finite domains, enabling mutex detection and causal-graph analysis.

name: Josephus problem
summary: Find the survivor when every k-th person is eliminated from a circle of n people.

name: Liveness-to-safety reduction
summary: Turn the search for an accepting cycle into an invariant check by adding a saved copy of the state and two flags; a bad state is a return to the saved state after an accepting one.

name: Bouton's theorem
summary: Theorem stating that a Nim position is losing for the player to move exactly when the xor of the pile sizes is zero.

name: Quantifier instantiation
summary: SMT solvers handle a formula forall x. phi by adding ground instances phi[x/t] to the quantifier-free problem. The choice of the terms t decides whether a proof is found.

name: Solved game
summary: Game whose game-theoretic value, and usually an optimal strategy, is known from start position.

name: Off-policy evaluation
summary: Estimate the value of a target policy from data logged by a different behavior policy, without running the target policy. Main methods: direct method, importance sampling, doubly robust.

name: Answer substitution
summary: A computed answer is the composition of the mgus of an SLD refutation, restricted to the query variables. Computed answers are correct, and every correct answer is an instance of one.

name: Syntax-guided synthesis
summary: Find a program from a given grammar that satisfies a logical specification.

name: Support vector regression
summary: Kernel regression that ignores errors smaller than ε and penalizes larger ones linearly. Its dual QP in α and α* gives a sparse fit; only points on or outside the tube count.

name: Clausal normal form
summary: A finite set of universally closed clauses that is satisfiable exactly when a given formula is. Distribution can make it exponential; definitions with new predicates keep it linear.

name: Conformant planning
summary: Find a plan that achieves the goal from every possible initial state, without sensing.

name: Ultrametric
summary: A distance with d(x, z) at most max(d(x, y), d(y, z)) for all x, y, z. On a finite set, ultrametrics are the same as monotone dendrograms.

name: Divisive clustering
summary: Top-down hierarchical clustering: start with one cluster and split clusters until each point is alone. DIANA splits off a splinter group at each step.

name: Futility pruning
summary: Skips moves near the leaves when the static evaluation plus a margin cannot raise alpha.

name: Paramodulation
summary: Inference rule for equality. It replaces a subterm that unifies with one side of an equation by the other side. With resolution, factoring and x = x it is refutation complete (Robinson and Wos 1969).

name: Cell decomposition
summary: Partitions free space into simple cells and searches the adjacency graph of cells.

name: Silhouette coefficient
summary: For each object, s = (b - a)/max(a, b): a is its mean distance to its own cluster, b to the nearest other cluster. The mean of s over all objects scores the clustering.

name: Jigsaw puzzle problem
summary: Reassemble pieces into the original picture from their edge compatibility; NP-hard in general.

name: UCPOP
summary: Partial-order planner supporting conditional effects and quantified goals.

name: Node consistency
summary: Every value in a variable's domain satisfies all unary constraints on that variable.

name: Nogood learning
summary: When a search for a CSP solution reaches a dead end, record the part of the current assignment that caused it as a nogood, a new constraint, so the search never repeats the same failure.

name: Multi-agent reinforcement learning
summary: Reinforcement learning with several agents that act in one environment. Each agent's world contains the others, who also learn, so the single-agent theory breaks and equilibria replace optima.

name: Term DAG
summary: Term representation with shared subterms, enabling efficient unification.

name: Pool adjacent violators algorithm
summary: Solve weighted isotonic regression in O(n) time with a stack of blocks; merge two adjacent blocks while their means violate the order.

name: Sliding puzzle solvability criterion
summary: A configuration is solvable exactly when the permutation parity matches the blank's row parity, for the odd-width case.

name: Automatic differentiation
summary: Exact derivatives of a program by the chain rule on its trace. Forward mode gives J v per run; reverse mode gives u^T J per run, so a gradient costs a few evaluations.

name: DRAT proof format
summary: Clausal proof of unsatisfiability as a list of added and deleted clauses; each added clause must be RUP or RAT, so every step keeps a satisfiable formula satisfiable.

name: Games on arbitrary graphs
summary: Two-player game played by moving a token along edges of a directed graph, analyzed by classifying positions as winning or losing.

name: Liveness property
summary: A property stating that something good eventually happens. No finite prefix can violate it, the liveness properties are the dense sets, and every property is safety intersected with liveness.

name: Evidence lower bound
summary: ELBO(q) = E_q[log p(x, z) - log q(z)]. It is at most log p(x), and the gap is exactly KL(q || p(z | x)).

name: Sequential minimal optimization
summary: Solves the soft margin SVM dual by optimizing two Lagrange multipliers at a time in closed form, chosen by Platt's heuristics, so no numerical QP solver is needed.

name: Fairness
summary: Constraints that keep only executions in which enabled actions are eventually taken. Weak fairness is justice, strong fairness is compassion, and fair CTL is checked with SCCs.

name: Manifold hypothesis
summary: High-dimensional data often lies near a low-dimensional manifold embedded in the ambient space.

name: Property specification patterns
summary: A catalogue of the temporal properties that occur again and again in practice, such as absence, response and precedence, each with a scope and ready-made formulas in LTL and CTL.

name: Weighted MaxSAT
summary: MaxSAT in which each clause has a positive weight. Find an assignment of largest total weight of true clauses, or equivalently of least total weight of false clauses.

name: Clause
summary: A finite set of literals read as their disjunction. It is true when one of its literals is true. Clauses are the units of CNF, of resolution and of SAT solvers.

name: Explained variance
summary: The fraction of the total variance that a principal component, or a subspace, captures: an eigenvalue of the covariance matrix divided by its trace.

name: Robinson completeness theorem
summary: A set of clauses is unsatisfiable if and only if binary resolution and factoring derive the empty clause from it (Robinson 1965). The proof joins Herbrand's theorem, ground completeness and lifting.

name: Hidden Markov model
summary: A Markov chain of hidden states, each of which emits one observed symbol. The parameters are the start, transition and emission probabilities (pi, A, B).

name: Régin's all-different filtering
summary: Filters the domains of an all-different constraint to generalized arc consistency with one maximum matching of the value graph and one strongly connected components pass, in O(n^(3/2) d) time.

name: Randomized PCA
summary: Find the top k principal components from a random sketch of the centered data: multiply by a Gaussian matrix, orthonormalize, do a few power steps, then take the SVD of a small matrix.

name: Latent semantic analysis
summary: Replace a weighted term-document matrix by its rank-k truncated SVD. Documents and folded-in queries become k-dimensional vectors that are compared by cosine similarity.

name: Plan-space planning
summary: Searches over partial plans, repairing open preconditions and threatened causal links.

name: Mini-batch k-means
summary: A stochastic k-means heuristic that updates the centers from small random batches, with per-center learning rate 1/count.

name: Computational graph
summary: A directed acyclic graph of primitive operations. Forward evaluation walks it in topological order; reverse mode differentiation walks it backward.

name: He initialization
summary: Draw each weight of a ReLU layer with mean 0 and variance 2/fan_in. ReLU keeps half of the second moment, and the factor 2 puts it back, so the signal neither grows nor fades.

name: Term indexing
summary: Data structures that retrieve, from a large set of terms or clauses, those that unify with, match, are instances of, or subsume a query.

name: Evaluation function
summary: Heuristic estimate of a position's value used at depth-limited leaves of a search.

name: Lookahead
summary: At each DPLL node, try every free variable both ways with unit propagation; fix failed literals and autarkies, and branch on the variable that reduces the formula most on both sides.

name: Reward function
summary: The part of an MDP that gives the scalar reward of each step, as R(s, a) or R(s, a, s'). The agent's goal is a large expected sum of these rewards.

name: Sprague-Grundy theorem
summary: Every impartial game position is equivalent to a Nim heap of size equal to its Grundy number.

name: Mean shift
summary: Move each point to the kernel weighted mean of the data around it, again and again, until it stops at a mode of the density; points at one mode form a cluster.

name: Statistical query model
summary: A learner that sees data only through estimates, within a tolerance tau, of expectations E[chi(x, c(x))]. SQ learners tolerate label noise; parity functions are not SQ learnable.

name: Counterfeit coin problem
summary: Identify a lighter or heavier fake coin among genuine ones using a balance in the fewest weighings.

name: Linear temporal logic
summary: A logic whose formulas talk about one infinite sequence of states, with the operators next, until and the derived eventually and always. A system satisfies a formula when every one of its paths does.

name: HMM decoding
summary: Find the hidden state path of highest probability given the observations of a hidden Markov model. A direct search has N^T paths; the Viterbi algorithm takes O(T N^2).

name: Alpha-beta pruning
summary: Minimax variant that keeps alpha and beta bounds and skips subtrees that cannot change the result.

name: Knuth-Moore theorem
summary: Gives the minimum number of leaves alpha-beta must evaluate on a uniform game tree with best move ordering.

name: Unifier
summary: A substitution that makes two terms, or all equations of a set, syntactically identical.

name: Higher-order unification problem
summary: Given two simply typed λ-terms whose free variables may stand for functions, find a substitution that makes them equal up to βη. The problem is undecidable from second order on.

name: Soft actor-critic
summary: Off-policy actor-critic for the maximum entropy objective: twin soft Q critics, a stochastic actor trained with reparameterized actions, and a temperature tuned to a target entropy.

name: Sequential Monte Carlo
summary: Weighted particles move through a sequence of targets by importance sampling with any proposal, and are resampled when the ESS 1/sum w_i^2 drops below a threshold.

name: Learning to rank
summary: Learn a scoring function from queries with graded documents, so that sorting by score puts relevant items first, as measured by NDCG. Pointwise, pairwise and listwise methods.

name: Trustworthiness and continuity
summary: Rank-based measures of how well an embedding preserves local neighbourhoods.

name: Consensus clustering
summary: Combines m clusterings into one that is near all of them: a median partition under the Mirkin distance, found by a majority pivot rule or by graph and hypergraph partitioning.

name: Data augmentation
summary: Train on randomly transformed copies of the examples, such as flips, crops, cutout or mixup. It acts as a regularizer and teaches the model invariances that the task has.

name: State explosion problem
summary: The number of states of a system grows exponentially with its processes and variables. It is the main limit of model checking, and every reduction only pushes it back.

name: Restarts in SAT solving
summary: A CDCL solver at times undoes all decisions and starts the search again, but keeps its learned clauses, scores and saved phases. A restart policy says when.

name: Unscented Kalman filter
summary: Approximate nonlinear filter that pushes 2n+1 weighted sigma points through f and h in place of Jacobians. Exact for linear maps; the mean is right to second order.

name: Kakuro problem
summary: Fill digits in a crossword-like grid so run sums and distinctness constraints hold; NP-complete.

name: Exponential BDD size for integer multiplication
summary: For every variable order, the OBDD of the middle bit of the product of two n-bit numbers has at least 2^(n/8) nodes (Bryant 1991). So no order makes BDDs of multipliers small.

name: Motion planning
summary: Find a collision-free path for a robot from a start configuration to a goal configuration.

name: Cover-Hart theorem
summary: As the sample grows, the 1-nearest-neighbor error R satisfies R* ≤ R ≤ R*(2 - M R*/(M - 1)) for M classes, so it is at most twice the Bayes error R*.

name: Open list
summary: The priority queue of generated but unexpanded states, ordered by f or h values.

name: Undecidability of second-order unification
summary: No algorithm decides second-order unification, even over one constant and one binary function symbol. Goldfarb proved it in 1981 by encoding Hilbert's tenth problem.

name: Minimum remaining values heuristic
summary: A dynamic variable ordering for backtracking search on a CSP. It assigns next the unassigned variable with the fewest values left in its current domain, a form of the fail-first principle.

name: Conjunctive normal form
summary: A formula that is a conjunction of clauses, each a disjunction of literals. Every Boolean function has one, and it is the input form of SAT solvers.

name: Parity game
summary: A two-player game of infinite duration on a finite graph. Player 0 wins a play when the largest priority seen infinitely often is even. Both players have positional winning strategies.

name: Subspace clustering problem
aliases: clustering in subspaces of high-dimensional data
summary: Find clusters that each live in their own subspace of a high-dimensional space: a subset of the attributes (axis-parallel) or any affine subspace (arbitrarily oriented).

name: Tower of Hanoi
summary: Move a stack of n disks between pegs under size constraints; optimal solution takes 2^n - 1 moves.

name: Bayesian network
summary: A DAG over random variables with one conditional distribution per node given its parents. The joint is their product; each node is independent of its non-descendants given its parents.

name: Elimination ordering
summary: The order in which variable elimination removes the variables. Its induced width sets the cost; the least width over all orders is the treewidth.

name: Hyperresolution
summary: Resolves all negative literals of a nucleus at once with positive electron clauses under one unifier, so every derived clause is positive. Refutation complete with factoring (Robinson 1965).

name: Assume-guarantee reasoning
summary: Check each component under an assumption about its environment, then discharge the assumption on the other components; non-circular rules are sound, circular ones need extra conditions.

name: Scree plot
summary: A plot of the eigenvalues of a covariance or correlation matrix in decreasing order. The elbow of the curve is a heuristic for the number of components to keep.

name: Loopy belief propagation
aliases: iterative belief propagation on graphs with cycles
summary: Run the sum-product messages of belief propagation on a factor graph with cycles until they stop changing. No convergence guarantee; fixed points are Bethe stationary points.

name: ReLU
summary: The activation function relu(x) = max(0, x): derivative 1 for x > 0 and 0 for x < 0, with f'(0) = 0 by convention; networks built from it are piecewise linear.

name: Residual belief propagation
summary: Loopy BP that always sends next the message whose new value differs most from its current one, found with a priority queue keyed by this residual.

name: Linear integer arithmetic satisfiability
summary: Decide satisfiability of linear constraints over the integers.

name: Standardization apart
summary: Renaming variables so that distinct clauses share no variables before unification.

name: Bias-variance tradeoff
summary: For squared loss, the expected error of a learned predictor at a point is exactly noise plus squared bias plus variance. More capacity often lowers bias and raises variance.

name: Fitted Q-iteration
summary: Batch reinforcement learning: regress the targets r + gamma max Q(s', b) on a fixed set of transitions, again and again. With a tabular regressor it is value iteration on the empirical MDP.

name: Loss function
summary: A loss scores one prediction against its label. Learning minimizes the mean loss; convex surrogates stand in for the 0-1 loss when they are classification calibrated.

name: Predicate abstraction
summary: Abstract an infinite or large system to a finite Boolean one whose state records which of n chosen predicates hold; abstract transitions come from decision procedure queries.

name: GSAT
summary: Greedy local search for SAT. From a random assignment, flip the variable that most increases the number of satisfied clauses, even if no flip helps; restart after MAX-FLIPS flips.

name: Policy iteration
summary: Alternate an exact evaluation of the current policy with a greedy improvement step until the policy no longer changes. The last policy is optimal.

name: Boolean equivalence checking
summary: Decide whether two boolean functions or circuits compute the same function.

name: Input resolution
summary: Resolution in which every step has an input clause as one parent. Complete for Horn clauses but not in general, and it refutes exactly the sets that unit resolution refutes (Chang 1970).

name: Representer theorem
summary: For any loss on the training values plus a strictly increasing function of the RKHS norm, every minimizer is a combination of the kernel functions k(x_i, ·).

name: Gap statistic
aliases: gap statistic for the number of clusters
summary: Gap(k) = E*[log W_k] - log W_k, with E* over uniform reference data. Choose the smallest k with Gap(k) >= Gap(k+1) - s_(k+1). It can return k = 1.

name: Hashiwokakero problem
summary: Connect numbered islands with bridges matching their degrees without crossings; NP-complete.

name: Rand index
summary: The share of the n(n-1)/2 pairs of objects on which two partitions agree, as together in both or apart in both. It is 1 only for equal partitions.

name: Minimax theorem
summary: In a finite two-player zero-sum game with mixed strategies, the maximin and minimax values are equal.

name: Knight's tour problem
summary: Find a sequence of knight moves visiting every square of a board exactly once.

name: MTD(f)
summary: Repeated null-window alpha-beta searches driven by a transposition table to converge on the minimax value.

name: DAgger
summary: Imitation learning that runs the learned policy, asks the expert to label the states it visits, adds them to one data set and retrains, so errors grow linearly, not quadratically, in T.

name: Potential-based reward shaping
summary: Add F(s, s') = gamma Phi(s') - Phi(s) to every reward. The optimal Q-values shift by exactly -Phi(s), so the optimal policies stay the same; no other shaping of this kind is safe.

name: Nash existence theorem
summary: Every finite game with mixed strategies has at least one Nash equilibrium.

name: Admissible heuristic
summary: A heuristic that never overestimates the true remaining cost to a goal.

name: Hybrid automata
summary: Automata whose real variables follow differential conditions in each mode and jump on mode switches. Reachability is undecidable even for linear flows and decidable for initialized rectangular ones.

name: CURE
summary: Agglomerative clustering in which each cluster keeps c scattered points shrunk toward its mean, and the closest pair of clusters by these points merges; sampling makes it scale.

name: Rapidly-exploring random tree
summary: Grows a tree from the start by extending toward random samples, biased to explore.

name: Bidirectional heuristic search
summary: Runs heuristic searches forward from the start and backward from the goal until they meet.

name: Multi-valued decision diagram
summary: An ordered decision diagram whose nodes branch on variables with finite domains of any size. Reduced MDDs are canonical, and they store the solution sets of finite-domain constraints.

name: Boolean satisfiability problem
summary: Decide whether a CNF formula has a satisfying assignment. The first problem shown NP-complete (Cook 1971, Levin 1973), and the target of CDCL solvers.

name: Retrograde analysis
summary: Works backward from terminal positions to label every position as win, loss or draw.

name: Kronecker-factored approximate curvature
summary: A natural gradient method for neural networks that approximates each layer's Fisher block by a Kronecker product of two small matrices, so the block inverse costs two small inverses.

name: MDP planning
summary: Given a finite MDP with known transitions and rewards, find an optimal policy and its values. Linear programming solves it in polynomial time, and it is P-complete.

name: Bounded variable elimination
summary: Eliminate a variable by replacing its clauses with all their non-tautological resolvents, but only when this does not make the formula larger; a model is rebuilt from the saved clauses.

name: MAX-2-SAT
summary: Satisfy as many 2-literal clauses as possible. NP-hard, unlike 2-SAT. Semidefinite rounding gives 0.878 (Goemans and Williamson), later about 0.940; above 21/22 is NP-hard.

name: Anti-unification problem
summary: Given terms, compute a least general generalization, the most specific pattern that has all of them as instances.

name: COP-k-means
aliases: constrained k-means of Wagstaff et al.
summary: K-means modified to respect must-link and cannot-link constraints.

name: Q-learning
summary: Off-policy TD control: move Q(S,A) toward R + gamma max_a Q(S',a). Tabular, with gamma < 1 and Robbins-Monro steps, it learns Q* under any policy that tries all pairs infinitely often.

name: Bit-vector satisfiability
summary: Decide constraints over fixed-width machine integers with bitwise and arithmetic operations.

name: LAMB optimizer
aliases: layer-wise adaptive moments optimizer for batch training
summary: Adam's normalized direction with decoupled weight decay, rescaled per layer so that each layer moves by the learning rate times its weight norm; built for very large batches.

name: Pruning (game trees)
summary: Discarding subtrees that provably cannot affect the minimax value of the root.

name: Ramification problem
summary: Deriving the indirect consequences of an action's direct effects.

name: Simple temporal problem
summary: Decide whether time points can meet constraints of the form a <= X_j - X_i <= b. It is consistent if and only if the distance graph has no negative cycle, and shortest paths give the minimal network.

name: Empirical risk minimization
summary: Choose a hypothesis from a fixed class with the least mean loss on the training sample. It learns well when the class has uniform convergence, but the search can be NP-hard.

name: SMT-LIB standard
summary: The common standard of SMT solvers. It defines a sorted first-order logic, a catalog of theories and logics, and a command language for scripts with push, pop, check-sat and get-model.

name: Deep deterministic policy gradient
summary: Off-policy actor-critic for continuous actions: a critic learned by Q-learning targets from replay, a deterministic actor moved along grad_a Q, slowly tracking target networks and noisy exploration.

name: Stochastic game
summary: Game in which chance moves, such as dice rolls, occur between player moves.

name: Dirichlet process
summary: A distribution over discrete distributions, used as a nonparametric prior for mixtures. Built by stick breaking or the Chinese restaurant process; for large n, n draws use about α log n clusters.

name: Nested depth-first search
summary: Find a reachable cycle through an accepting state of a Büchi automaton, or of the product of a system with one, with two interleaved depth-first searches in linear time and two extra bits per state.

name: Bayesian inference
summary: Treat unknown parameters as random. Combine a prior with the likelihood of the data by Bayes' theorem to get a posterior, and predict by averaging over it.

name: Rubik's Cube problem
summary: Find a move sequence that solves a scrambled Rubik's Cube; the search space has about 4.3 * 10^19 states.

name: Stateless model checking
summary: Check a concurrent program by running it again and again under a controlled scheduler, one interleaving per run, without storing any program state; reductions cut the number of runs.

name: Activation function
summary: The scalar nonlinear function f applied to each unit after the linear map of a layer, a = f(Wx + b): sigmoid, tanh, ReLU, GELU and others.

name: Temporal planning
summary: Planning with durative actions, concurrency and explicit time constraints.

name: Cofactor
summary: The function obtained from f by fixing one variable to 0 or 1.

name: Automata-theoretic approach
summary: Treat the system and the negated property as automata on infinite words, so that verification becomes emptiness of their product, a search for a reachable accepting cycle.

name: ROC curve and AUC
summary: The ROC curve plots true positive rate against false positive rate over all thresholds. Its area equals U/(n+ n-), the rate of correctly ordered pairs.

name: Paterson-Wegman linear unification
summary: Linear-time unification of terms represented as shared DAGs.

name: Core-guided MaxSAT
summary: Solves MaxSAT with a SAT solver. Each unsatisfiable core of soft clauses gets relaxation variables and an exactly-one constraint, and adds 1 to a lower bound that ends at the optimum.

name: Learning real-time A*
summary: Real-time search in unknown spaces that learns heuristic values from experience.

name: Effective branching factor
summary: The branching factor b* of a uniform tree that would generate the same number of nodes as a search, used to measure heuristic quality.

name: k-median problem
summary: Choose k centers minimizing the total (not squared) distance from points to their nearest center.

name: Extended Kalman filter
aliases: linearized Kalman filter for nonlinear models
summary: Approximate filter for nonlinear state space models: run the Kalman filter on the model linearized with Jacobians at the current estimate. Exact only for linear models.

name: Conflict-based search
summary: Optimal multi-agent pathfinding by a two-level search over path constraints that resolve conflicts.

name: Binary decision diagram
summary: A rooted DAG of decision nodes that test variables and represent a boolean function.

name: Dyna-Q
summary: After each real step, do a Q-learning update, store the transition in a table model, and do n more Q-learning updates on transitions replayed from the model.

name: Sleep sets
summary: In a search of interleavings, carry along the transitions that an earlier branch already explored and that nothing since has disturbed, and skip them, so that equivalent orders are not explored twice.

name: Resampling
summary: Replace N weighted particles by N equally weighted copies, particle i copied N w_i times on average. Multinomial, residual, stratified and systematic schemes.

name: Magic square problem
summary: Fill an n-by-n grid with distinct integers so every row, column and diagonal has the same sum.

name: Structured prediction
summary: Learn to predict outputs with internal structure, such as tag sequences, parse trees or matchings, by scoring whole outputs and decoding the best one, for example with Viterbi.

name: Task network
summary: A set of tasks with ordering and variable-binding constraints, the unit of HTN decomposition.

name: Planning Domain Definition Language
summary: Standard input language for planning domains and problems, used in the planning competitions.

name: Free binary decision diagram
summary: A BDD in which each path tests each variable at most once, but different paths may use different orders. It allows linear-time counting and a randomized equivalence test.

name: Literal block distance
summary: The number of distinct decision levels among the literals of a learned clause. CDCL solvers use it to rank learned clauses for deletion and to time restarts.

name: Isotonic regression
summary: Find the non-decreasing sequence nearest to given values in weighted squared error. The solution is unique and has a max-min formula.

name: Pushdown reachability
summary: Decide whether a pushdown system can go from one configuration, or regular set of configurations, to another. Solvable in cubic time by saturation; P-complete.

name: Conditional effects
summary: Action effects that apply only when a given condition holds in the state.

name: Natural policy gradient
summary: Policy gradient ascent along F^-1 grad J, where F is the Fisher matrix of the policy averaged over visited states; for a softmax policy the step is the compatible critic's weights.

name: Water jug problem
