summary: Replans efficiently when edge costs change during travel, reusing previous search effort.

name: If-then-else (ITE) operator
summary: Computes if f then g else h on BDDs and thereby implements all binary and unary operators.

name: Lifelong planning A*
summary: Incremental A* that repairs previous search results when graph edge costs change.

name: Real-time dynamic programming
summary: Trial-based value updates along simulated trajectories, focusing effort on relevant states.

name: Maximum entropy reinforcement learning
summary: Reinforcement learning whose objective adds alpha times the policy entropy to every reward. The soft Bellman equation uses a log-sum-exp, and the best policy is a softmax of Q / alpha.

name: Maximum-spacing k-clustering
summary: Partition n points into k nonempty clusters so that the least distance between two points in different clusters is as large as possible.

name: Equivalence of weak and strong learnability
summary: A class is PAC learnable if and only if some efficient learner always does slightly better than random guessing. Boosting turns such a weak learner into a strong one.

name: Do-calculus
summary: Three rules, each with a d-separation test in a cut graph, that rewrite interventional probabilities. They are sound, and complete for identifying causal effects.

name: Canonicity of reduced ordered BDDs
summary: For a fixed order each boolean function has exactly one ROBDD, so equivalence is a pointer comparison.

name: Counterfactual regret minimization
summary: Iterative self-play method whose average strategy converges to a Nash equilibrium in two-player zero-sum games.

name: Knaster-Tarski theorem
summary: Every monotone function on a complete lattice has a least and a greatest fixed point, and its fixed points form a complete lattice. It gives the semantics of the modal mu-calculus.

name: Factor graph
summary: A bipartite graph of variable nodes and factor nodes for g(x) = product of local factors. It shows any BN or MRF factorization exactly; sum-product on a tree gives exact marginals.

name: Lights Out puzzle
summary: Toggle lights on a grid to turn all of them off; solvable by linear algebra over GF(2).

name: VSIDS branching heuristic
summary: Branch on the free variable with the highest activity. Each conflict raises the activity of the variables involved in it, and old increments fade by a constant factor.

name: Negamax
summary: Compact form of minimax using the identity max(a,b)=-min(-a,-b) for zero-sum games.

name: Presburger arithmetic
aliases: first-order theory of the integers with addition
summary: First-order theory of the natural numbers with addition, decidable by quantifier elimination.

name: Hierarchical pathfinding A*
summary: Plans on an abstracted cluster graph first, then refines the path locally.

name: First unique implication point
summary: The unique implication point nearest to the conflict in the implication graph. The cut there gives the standard learned clause of CDCL, with one literal of the conflict level.

name: Logistic loss
summary: The margin loss log(1 + exp(-y f)) for labels in {-1, +1}. It equals binary cross-entropy with labels in {0, 1}, is convex and smooth, and its minimizer is the log-odds.

name: Regression
summary: Learn a function that predicts a real number from an input. Under squared loss the best possible predictor is the conditional mean of the output given the input.

name: Value iteration
summary: Apply the Bellman optimality backup to every state again and again. The values converge geometrically to V*, and the greedy policy of the last values is eps-optimal.

name: History heuristic
summary: Move ordering scoring each move by how often it caused cutoffs across the whole search.

name: LRAT proof format
summary: Clausal proof format in which each added clause lists the IDs of the clauses that make it RUP or RAT, so a checker needs no search and runs in time linear in the hinted proof.

name: Singleton arc consistency
summary: Arc consistency holds after restricting each variable to a single value in turn.

name: Labelled transition system
summary: A set of states with transitions labelled by actions, the standard model of process calculi; it puts the information on the edges where a Kripke structure puts it on the states.

name: Occam's razor in learning
summary: A consistent hypothesis that can be written in few bits generalizes: with probability 1 - delta its true error is at most (|h| ln 2 + ln(1/delta))/n.

name: Huet's almost-linear unification
summary: First-order unification on a term DAG. Union-find merges the classes of nodes that must be equal, and one cycle test at the end does the occurs check. It runs in O(N α(N)) time.

name: Plan recognition
summary: Infer an agent's goal or plan from observations of its actions.

name: Heuristic dominance
summary: H1 dominates h2 when h1(n) >= h2(n) for all states, both admissible; the more informed one prunes more.

name: State space
summary: The graph of states reachable from a start state by applying actions, with edge costs.

name: Limited discrepancy search
summary: Explores paths that deviate from the heuristic's choice in at most k places, in increasing k.

name: Best move selection
summary: Choose a move from a position that is best under the search's evaluation within a time budget.

name: Learned clause minimization
summary: Remove from a first-UIP learned clause every literal whose value follows, through reason clauses, from the other literals of the clause. The result is shorter, still implied and still asserting.

name: Retrace
summary: Off-policy multi-step learning of Q with traces c = lambda min(1, pi/mu). The operator is a gamma-contraction to Q^pi for any behavior policy, with no trace cut on-policy.

name: Bellman equation
summary: Recursive equation characterizing optimal value functions of an MDP.

name: Gradient clipping
summary: Rescale the gradient when its norm exceeds a threshold c, g ← g·min(1, c/‖g‖), so a step keeps its direction but has bounded length; clipping each entry instead changes the direction.

name: Hidden semi-Markov model
summary: An HMM in which each visit to a state lasts for a duration drawn from an explicit distribution, in place of the geometric durations of an HMM.

name: Clause subsumption
summary: Remove each clause that contains another clause, and shorten a clause when a resolvent subsumes it; both steps keep the formula logically equivalent.

name: Imperfect-information game
summary: Game in which players have private or hidden information, such as cards held in hand.

name: Fringe search
summary: A* variant that keeps the open list as a doubly linked list, avoiding a heap with similar performance.

name: Real-time A*
summary: Bounded-lookahead real-time search that moves toward the best successor and updates heuristic values.

name: Dynamic Bayesian network
summary: A Bayesian network that repeats over time slices, given by a prior net and a two-slice net. HMMs and linear dynamical systems are special cases.

name: God's number
aliases: God's number for the Rubik's Cube
summary: The maximum over all scrambles of the minimum number of moves needed to solve the cube; shown to be 20 in the half-turn metric.

name: Fuzzy c-means
summary: Soft clustering in which each point has a graded membership in every cluster.

name: LTL model checking
summary: Decide whether every path of a finite Kripke structure satisfies an LTL formula, and give a lasso-shaped counterexample when one does not. It takes O(|M| 2^O(|φ|)) time and is PSPACE-complete.

name: Domino tiling problem
summary: Count or find ways to cover a board with dominoes; counting is polynomial via Kasteleyn's method for planar boards.

name: Missionaries and cannibals problem
summary: Ferry missionaries and cannibals across a river without letting cannibals outnumber missionaries on either bank.

name: Linear programming formulation of MDPs
summary: Write a finite MDP as a linear program: the primal over values, the dual over occupancy measures. Solve it with the simplex method and read the policy from the dual.

name: Decision diagram
summary: Compact graph representation of Boolean or finite-domain functions used for symbolic state sets.

name: Neural architecture search
summary: Search a space of network architectures for one with the best validation performance. Methods differ in search space, search strategy (RL, evolution, DARTS) and performance estimation.

name: Mercer's theorem
summary: A continuous, symmetric, positive semidefinite kernel on a compact domain has an eigen-expansion with nonnegative eigenvalues that converges absolutely and uniformly.

name: Constraint satisfaction problem
summary: Assign values from finite domains to variables so that every constraint over subsets of variables is satisfied.

name: Set-of-support strategy
summary: Resolution in which every step needs a parent from a chosen support set or derived from it. It is complete when the clauses outside the support are satisfiable (Wos, Robinson and Carson 1965).

name: Satisfiability threshold
summary: The clause-to-variable ratio at which random k-SAT jumps from satisfiable to unsatisfiable. Sharp (Friedgut 1999); exactly 1 for k = 2; located for large k by Ding, Sly and Sun.

name: Contraction property of the Bellman operator
summary: For a discount gamma < 1, the Bellman operators T^pi and T* are gamma-contractions in the max norm. So each has one fixed point, and value iteration converges geometrically.

name: Rauch-Tung-Striebel smoother
summary: Exact fixed-interval smoother for linear Gaussian state space models: a Kalman filter forward pass, then a backward pass with gain C_t = P_t|t A^T P_(t+1|t)^(-1).

name: Rapid action value estimation
summary: MCTS enhancement sharing action value statistics across subtrees to speed early learning.

name: Principal variation
summary: Best line of play found by the search, from the root to a leaf.

name: Symmetry breaking
summary: Adds constraints or search rules that remove solutions equivalent under a symmetry, so that search explores each symmetry class once. Lex-leader constraints keep at least one solution in every class.

name: Optimal planning
summary: Find a plan of minimum total action cost.

name: Structural causal model
summary: Each variable is a function of its direct causes and an exogenous noise. Replacing equations gives interventions, and fixing the noise gives counterfactuals.

name: Duplicate detection
summary: Recognising states reached by multiple paths so each is expanded once, trading memory for time.

name: Completeness threshold
summary: A bound k such that, if bounded model checking finds no counterexample of length at most k, the property holds; the diameter and the recurrence diameter bound it for safety.

name: PATHMAX
summary: Propagates the parent f-value to children so an inconsistent admissible heuristic behaves monotonically.

name: Delta-satisfiability
summary: Decide that a formula is unsatisfiable or that its delta-weakening is satisfiable, with bounded numeric error.

name: Twenty questions problem
summary: Identify an unknown object from yes or no answers; the information bound gives log2 of the number of candidates.

name: Extremely randomized trees
summary: An ensemble of trees grown on the whole sample, where each node draws K attributes and one random cut point for each, and keeps the best of these K splits by score.

name: k-induction
summary: Prove an invariant with two SAT checks per depth k, a BMC base case and an induction step over any k + 1 good states; simple-path constraints make it complete for finite systems.

name: Variable elimination
summary: Exact inference: multiply the factors that hold a variable, sum the variable out, repeat. Time O(n d^(w+1)) for an order of induced width w.

name: Satisfiability modulo theories (SMT) problem
summary: Decide whether a formula with Boolean structure over atoms of background theories, such as arithmetic, arrays or bit-vectors, has a model in which those theories hold.

name: Policy improvement theorem
summary: If a policy pi' does at least as well as pi for one step in every state, judged by Q^pi, then V^pi' >= V^pi everywhere, strictly where the one-step gain is positive.

name: Layer-wise adaptive rate scaling
summary: Gives each layer the learning rate eta times its weight norm over its gradient norm, so every layer changes by the same fraction per step; used for large batch SGD.

name: AC-4 algorithm
summary: Enforces arc consistency in optimal O(ed^2) time by maintaining support counters and lists of supported values.

name: Clause database reduction
summary: The policy by which a CDCL solver deletes part of its learned clauses at set times, ranked by LBD, activity or size, so that propagation stays fast. Clauses that are reasons are kept.

name: Clause subsumption
summary: A clause C subsumes D if some substitution maps C into a subset of D. Then C implies D, and provers delete D. Testing it is NP-complete; deletion keeps resolution complete.

name: Contrastive divergence
summary: Train an RBM by replacing the model expectation in the log likelihood gradient with k Gibbs steps started at the data. Cheap and biased; it is not the gradient of any function.

name: Stuttering equivalence
summary: An equivalence that ignores finite repetitions of the same label along paths; for finite Kripke structures it coincides with agreement on all CTL* formulas without the next operator.

name: Minimax-Q
summary: Q-learning for two-player zero-sum Markov games: Q(s, a, o) holds both players' actions, and the max in the target is replaced by the value of the matrix game Q(s', ., .), solved by a linear program.

name: Relaxed planning graph
summary: Planning graph built with delete effects ignored, used to extract relaxed plans.

name: Peg solitaire
summary: Remove pegs by jumping over them until a single peg remains.

name: State value function
summary: V^pi(s): the expected discounted return from state s when the agent follows the policy pi. V*(s) is the largest such value over all policies.

name: Consistent heuristic
summary: A heuristic satisfying h(n) <= c(n,n') + h(n') for every edge; implies admissibility and monotone f-values.

name: Partial MaxSAT
summary: Clauses are hard or soft. Find an assignment that satisfies every hard clause and the most soft clauses (or the most soft weight). No approximation ratio is possible unless P = NP.

name: Robinson's resolution principle
summary: Refute first-order clauses by adding factors and binary resolvents, built with most general unifiers, until the empty clause appears. Sound and refutation complete (Robinson 1965).
